metadata.basis: Protected UNI source definitions and hierarchy, pinned IFC 4.3.2 catalogue, and mapping policy D01-D09

disposition_meaning.accept: The existing proposal is defensible under its recorded condition.
disposition_meaning.revise: The proposal was changed in mapping-proposals.json.
disposition_meaning.needs_user: UNI scope or intended IFC modelling practice cannot be established from available evidence.

1.2.3.reason: IfcElementAssembly has direct frame and truss types. Individual beams and members are components, not spatial structures.

1.3.0.reason: The UNI definition explicitly concerns resisting earth loads. Retaining walls and structural slabs can directly perform that role under the stated condition.

1.3.2.reason: A horizontal structural slab can resist earth loads; the condition must exclude ordinary floors and roof slabs.

2.2.2.reason: The source has no definition. IFC distinguishes trapdoors and windows, but the intended range of lower horizontal closures is not documented.

3.0.0.reason: The UNI aggregate covers several kinds of internal subdivision; the catalogue has no concrete system occurrence with that direct scope. Empty is defensible.

3.1.3.reason: IfcRailing protects users; IfcImpactProtectionDevice protects built elements. The undefined UNI leaf does not establish whether both are intended.

3.2.3.reason: IfcDoor/TRAPDOOR directly represents an internal horizontal opening closure.

4.0.0.reason: The source aggregate spans external space division in several orientations; no concrete IFC system occurrence matches it directly. Empty is defensible.

4.1.0.reason: Walls, boundary railings and gates can themselves divide external space when the recorded site-boundary role applies.

4.2.0.reason: A slab can directly form an external horizontal platform or subdivision under the recorded role condition.

4.2.2.reason: IfcSlab can form the deck of an elevated walkway; this selection excludes railings and other possible components.

5.1.1.reason: The undefined Alimentazione leaf does not say whether HVAC supply means fuel, thermal fluid, electric power, or a subset.

5.1.3.reason: Air handlers, chillers, cooling towers and heat exchangers directly treat HVAC air or liquid; retain only occurrences actually serving this central function.

5.4.1.reason: The undefined Alimentazione leaf does not establish whether this is the electrical feed or another input to the aeriform-disposal system.

5.5.0.reason: IfcDistributionSystem has MUNICIPALSOLIDWASTE and DISPOSAL types; the UNI definition explicitly includes removal and accumulation of solid waste.

5.5.2.reason: IfcDuctSegment can form a ventilation shaft. IfcChimney is defined for combustion flues, and IfcStackTerminal represents a cap/terminal rather than the shaft.

5.7.1.reason: The undefined electrical Alimentazione leaf does not establish whether the main board is supply or distribution, or which generation and storage equipment belongs here.

5.8.1.reason: The undefined telecommunications Alimentazione leaf could mean incoming signal/media or electrical power for equipment; these imply different IFC selections.

5.9.1.reason: The undefined transport Alimentazione leaf does not establish whether it includes the drive motor and connection, or only incoming power supply.

5.9.3.reason: IfcTransportElement may represent the complete machine, while IfcConveyorSegment is a system segment. The intended modelling of Parti mobili is unspecified.

6.2.2.reason: IFC has no dedicated earth-electrode entity; whether an electrode is modelled as IfcCableSegment/CONDUCTORSEGMENT is a project convention.

6.3.1.reason: Whether lightning air-termination elements are modelled as IfcCableSegment/CONDUCTORSEGMENT is a project convention.

6.3.3.reason: Whether lightning earth electrodes are modelled as IfcCableSegment/CONDUCTORSEGMENT is a project convention.

6.4.1.reason: Dedicated power cabling and a battery or UPS can directly supply the anti-intrusion system under the recorded condition.

7.0.0.reason: An internal furnishing occurrence can directly receive the broad internal-equipment code; the mapping need not cover every descendant kind.

7.1.1.reason: IfcFurniture can represent a complete storage cabinet or wall. IfcSystemFurnitureElement/PANEL is a component of modular furniture.

7.2.0.reason: The source defines an aggregated service block, but does not establish whether a governed IfcElementAssembly convention exists or an empty mapping is intended.

8.0.0.reason: An outdoor furnishing can directly receive the broad external-equipment code, although IfcFurnishingElement does not cover fences or pavements. Clarified the condition.

8.2.0.reason: The source aggregate includes outdoor installations and boundaries; fences and pavements are separately mapped at child level. No single concrete occurrence covers this aggregate.
